summary:
Kebbi is one of twelve northern Nigerian states that adopted criminal Shari'a in the wave that began with Zamfara's Shari'a Establishment Law (enacted 27 October 1999, in force 27 January 2000). By 2002 Kebbi had Shari'a criminal legislation and Shari'a courts with criminal jurisdiction over Muslims, a jurisdiction no other Nigerian state outside this bloc holds.

Kebbi's own statute is the Penal Code (Amendment) Law (Law No. 21 of 2000), signed and brought into operation on 1 December 2000 and published in Kebbi State Gazette Vol. 2 No. 1 (Supplement, 31 December 2000). Its enacted text provides that whoever commits the offence of sodomy shall be punished with stoning to death (rajm). Kebbi is one of only three states, with Kaduna and Katsina, whose written law carries that capital wording for men's acts.

The same Kebbi statute criminalises same-sex acts between women with up to 50 lashes and imprisonment of up to six months. The UK Home Office country note of June 2025 carries Kebbi's own row in its twelve-state Shari'a penalties table (section 8.4.3) recording these penalties, confirming that Kebbi's Shari'a layer extends criminalisation to conduct between women and leaves the state's code broader in scope and harsher than the federal SSMPA for Muslim defendants.

Wikipedia's coverage places Kebbi inside the northern Shari'a block where same-sex acts carry penalties ranging up to capital punishment, and notes that death penalties for lesbianism are applied only in Kano and Katsina, placing Kebbi in the lashing-and-imprisonment tier for women's conduct, consistent with Kebbi's own statute. The same coverage records a cross-dressing layer in the north: prison or a fine for men who dress or behave as women, with a Kano court imposing one year's imprisonment in 2025 under Kano's provision allowing up to one year or a fine.

The cross-dressing provision is a Kano rule, not a Kebbi one; no equivalent Kebbi cross-dressing statute is documented in these sources. No housing, segregation or placement rule for trans prisoners in Kebbi or elsewhere in Nigeria is recorded in the sources reviewed.
tangentialFactors:
Kebbi's Shari'a layer sits on top of the national SSMPA regime, so a trans visitor faces both the federal 10-to-14-year exposure and, as a Muslim subject to state Shari'a jurisdiction, the state's own capital and corporal penalties. The two layers are cumulative rather than alternative.

The federal Criminal Code and the northern Shari'a block are described in general sources alongside Kebbi, but the Kebbi-specific findings above are drawn from the state's own enacted text and the Home Office table row.

The 2022 proposals to criminalise cross-dressing nationally, and the 2025 Kano sentence of a TikToker to one year, indicate an active legislative and judicial direction of travel in the north on gender presentation, though no Kebbi cross-dressing statute is documented.
localsOnly:
Residents of Kebbi who are Muslim fall under the state's Shari'a criminal jurisdiction, exercised by Shari'a courts, in addition to the ordinary courts. The state's Penal Code (Amendment) Law 2000 has been in operation since 1 December 2000.

Women in Kebbi face up to 50 lashes and six months' imprisonment for same-sex acts under the state statute, a penalty bloc shared with other northern states rather than the Kano/Katsina capital maximum. Men face stoning to death under the same enacted text.

The sources reviewed contain no Kebbi-specific record of arrests, prosecutions, venue closures, police practice, or trans-prisoner placement decisions within the state.
outOfScopeNotes:
Whether Kebbi's capital sodomy provision has ever been carried out, or is currently applied, is unresolved in the sources reviewed; the inventory documents the enacted text and its penalties but no Kebbi execution or sentence under it.

No Kebbi-specific incidents of violence against trans people, police extortion, dating-app entrapment, or healthcare access barriers are documented in this inventory; the national pattern is carried by the parent record and is not restated here.

Whether Kebbi has adopted any cross-dressing or gender-presentation offence of its own, as Kano has, is not sourced; the reviewed material attributes that provision to Kano alone.

The interaction between Kebbi's Shari'a courts and federal SSMPA proceedings for the same conduct, and which forum would take a case against a visitor, is not addressed in the sources.
